title: Same-Class Minimax Converse for Pointwise CATE under Exactly Uniform Design
banked_reason: D0.5.G: mathematically complete matched fixed-n converse, but the strict exact-uniform Bernoulli subclass scores 6.9 below the 7.2 field floor because the upper-rate phenomenon is already published.
gap_reasons: Its contribution is nevertheless confined to resolving the converse on a strict, highly structured subclass for which the corresponding upper-rate phenomenon was already published, so it does not establish a new general CATE frontier.
The practical interpretation is only a precision benchmark: the paper supplies neither adaptation nor inference nor evidence that the cited forest and R-learner workflows attain the rate.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.9 < 7.2, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: The run completed the missing same-class fixed-n converse using exact singleton cancellation, geometric component factorization, a mixed-amplitude Hellinger bound, and a spanning-tree sum, matching it to a total estimator for every fixed known x0 throughout S <= S_star, including the no-log elbow. Both mathematical review panels passed with no findings; the result was downgraded only because its strict exact-uniform Bernoulli subclass and already-published upper-rate phenomenon did not meet the field-level breadth/significance threshold.
tldr: For every fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), the exact-uniform bounded-overlap Bernoulli model has sharp pointwise CATE risk \(R_n\asymp n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\) throughout \(S=\alpha+\beta\le d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\). A reflected inward local projection estimator attains the rate on every data set, and a translated correlated-sign component prior proves the genuine fixed-\(n\) same-class converse. At the elbow the rate is exactly \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), with no logarithmic multiplier; strictly below it, nuisance learning causes an unavoidable slower power.
gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE supplies the candidate below-elbow rate and higher-order estimator, but its displayed hard laws remove covariate mass from nuisance-bump transition regions. A lower bound over that larger density model does not imply the same bound after fixing the design to exact uniformity, and the partition-local theorem of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax does not apply verbatim to overlapping smooth frames.
fill: The paper develops a correlated-sign smooth-frame prior and conditions on the observed covariates to factor its likelihood over sparse overlap components. A uniform component Hellinger inequality and random-geometric spanning-tree sum yield the missing nuisance-rate lower bound, while an explicit clipped projection U-statistic supplies the matching total upper bound.
